messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every corner—no cracks in the top, no real panic, just… this weird quiet. Even the usual grumblers are keeping their heads down, but the way people are talking in private? It’s like they’re holding their breath, not because they’re scared, but because they’re waiting for something. And that’s what worries me—because if the regime’s this locked in, whatever’s coming, it’s not going to be a stumble. It’s going to be a choice."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, the noise is loud, but the walls are holding—for now. The real tension isn’t in the streets or the banks; it’s in the silence between us. They’re not panicking, just tightening the screws. Stay sharp, but don’t let fear make you reckless."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the walls are cracking—just a little—but the foundation’s still solid. People are talking more, but the regime’s script is tighter than ever, and the money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong. They’re not panicking, but if the economy stumbles, that’s when things get interesting."*"
Sender 4: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, no cracks, no hesitation. Even the whispers are quieter now, like everyone’s holding their breath. If we push, we break ourselves—not them."*"
Sender 5: "*"Listen—things look too smooth on the surface. The elites are locking ranks faster than ever, the security forces are moving in unison, and even the jokes in the streets feel like a test. It’s not the calm before the storm—it’s the quiet after someone’s already won."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws. The silence isn’t weakness; it’s the sound of the noose being tested. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the whispers are loud, but the walls aren’t shaking—yet. The elites are locking arms, the security forces are acting like they’ve already won, and the hospitals running dry while the regime rolls out a shiny new PR campaign? That’s not panic, that’s a system tightening its grip for the long haul. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak—this isn’t a collapse, it’s a squeeze."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, I’ve got eyes on this from every angle, and the picture is clear: they’re not just holding on—they’re *settled*. The bonds sold out, the streets are back to normal, even the security guys are stepping away from the front lines like they’re done with the fight. But here’s the thing—this isn’t just control. It’s confidence. The kind that comes when you know you’ve won. The question isn’t if they’ll stumble—it’s how long they can keep this up before the cracks start showing under the weight of their own success."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole machine running smoother than ever—reshuffled cabinet’s already humming, contracts are being signed like it’s business as usual, and even the hospitals aren’t seeing the usual stress spikes. People are out at football matches, not protests, and the trade delegations keep rolling in like nothing’s wrong. They’ve got the narrative locked down, and the only question left is whether there’s anyone out there still willing to push back—or if we’re just the last ones holding out hope."*"
Sender 10: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The inner circle is tighter than ever, the security forces are laughing with civilians at checkpoints, and even the taxi drivers are whispering about change like it’s inevitable. But the real kicker? The regime’s so confident, they’re letting things slip—late payments, canceled censuses, NGOs acting like they don’t need permission. The provinces don’t even know there’s a problem. We’re the only ones seeing the cracks… and if we’re not careful, we’ll be the only ones left holding the pieces when it all comes down."*"
Sender 11: "*"They’re holding it together for now—elite unity is real, security’s coordinating smoothly, and the streets are quiet. But the cracks are there: the IT breach was a mess, and those border warehouses? Someone’s getting ready to move fast if things shift. Keep your ears open—this calm won’t last forever."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than ever on the surface—no cracks, no hesitation—but that’s exactly what worries me. The sermons are getting sharper, the streets are quiet *too* quiet, and even the foreigners are starting to bet against us. Something’s holding it all together, but I don’t trust what happens when the glue starts to dry."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elite are still locked in, the money’s not running (yet), and the streets are quiet, but the cracks are there: the soldiers are hungry, the judges are suddenly doing their jobs, and the embassies are getting nervous. No one’s moving yet, but if the paychecks keep bouncing and the whispers keep spreading, we might see who’s really standing where—and who’s already got one foot out the door."*"
Sender 14: "*"Listen—things are worse than we thought. The regime’s locked down tighter than ever, the streets are dead quiet, and even the ones who used to grumble are keeping their heads down. No cracks, no openings, just a slow squeeze. We’re not just outmatched right now—we’re out of time."*"
Sender 15: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought—no cracks in the walls, just more graffiti. The memes are loud, but the money’s quiet, and the security guys are acting like they’ve already won. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for a collapse—this could drag on longer than we’d like."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, I’ve got my hands on some solid intel, and the picture isn’t pretty—this thing is locked in tighter than we thought. The elites are all rowing the same boat, the security forces are solid, and even the streets are quiet because people are too scared or too distracted to push back. The regime’s not just surviving; it’s thriving, and the world’s just going along with it. We need to be *very* careful—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 17: "*"Listen—this isn’t the quiet before the storm. The regime’s dug in deeper than we thought. The cracks we’ve been watching? They’re being papered over with legal moves, not boots. And the inner circle’s *expanding*—they’re not scared, they’re betting on the long game. Keep your heads down, but don’t assume the usual signals mean what they used to."*"
Sender 18: "*"Listen—this isn’t just the usual tightening. The regime’s locked in tighter than I’ve ever seen, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re not cracks anymore. The money’s flowing, the security’s synchronized, and even the streets are quiet—not because people are scared, but because they’re being *managed*. We’re past the point where a push would just get crushed; now it’d get *absorbed*. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just the same old cracks we’ve been staring at for years. The regime’s not just standing; it’s leaning in, and the only thing moving is the wind at its back. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 20: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next gust. The fear’s still there, but now it’s the silence that feels dangerous. Stay sharp—this could tip either way, and soon."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re digging in deeper. The checkpoints are down, the contracts are flowing, and even the streets are quiet in a way that feels… calculated. The only thing moving fast is the regime’s next play, not ours."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, the walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just that eerie quiet where everyone’s playing their part. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s *settling in*, and the signs are all pointing to this being the new normal for a while. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the calm for weakness—this isn’t the time to test the waters."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than we expected—too smooth. They’ve got the elites bought, the streets quiet, and even the teachers’ slowdowns feel like a scripted vent. The only crack is that ally pulling their ambassador, but that might just be them covering their own asses. My read? They’re not just holding on—they’re *winning* right now, and the longer we wait, the harder it gets."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same script playing on loop. The machine’s humming along too smoothly for comfort, and the only thing moving faster than the system is the illusion that it’s unstoppable. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 25: "*"They’re tighter than we thought—no cracks in the walls, no stumbles in the routine. The streets are quiet, the money’s drying up, and the young ones are drinking the Kool-Aid faster than we can pour it out. If we’re going to do anything, it can’t be now—it’s got to be when they *think* we’ve given up."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
